purpose: Levothyroxine is used to treat an underactive thyroid gland, a condition called hypothyroidism. Your thyroid gland normally makes a hormone that controls your energy, metabolism, and many body functions. When it does not make enough on its own, this medication replaces it.
how_it_works: Your thyroid naturally produces a hormone called T4, and levothyroxine is actually a man-made version of that exact hormone. Once you swallow the pill, your body absorbs it and converts it into the active form your cells need to keep your metabolism running smoothly. Think of it as simply refilling what your thyroid is missing.
common_side_effects: Most people tolerate this medication very well when the dose is right. If the dose is too high, you may notice a fast or pounding heartbeat, feeling shaky or nervous, trouble sleeping, increased sweating, feeling too warm, or unintended weight loss. These usually mean your dose needs to be adjusted.
warnings: Never stop taking this medication without talking to your doctor, even if you feel fine — your body needs it every day. Take it on an empty stomach, ideally 30 to 60 minutes before breakfast, with a full glass of water. Many common things like calcium supplements, antacids, iron, and even coffee can block the medication from being absorbed properly, so space these out by at least 4 hours. Tell your doctor right away if you have chest pain or a very fast heartbeat.
typical_dosing: Most adults start at a low dose, often between 25 and 50 micrograms once daily, taken in the morning on an empty stomach. Your doctor will gradually adjust your dose based on blood test results until your thyroid hormone levels are in a healthy range. The average maintenance dose for most adults is between 100 and 200 micrograms per day, but your dose is very personal and based on your specific needs.
